Due to some problems with my email yesterday, I may not have received your 
RSVP.....please excuse any confusion this may have caused.


RSVP REQUESTED!

The Environmental Strategies Group will convene an "Emissions Strategy 
Meeting" on Friday, May 18 to discuss global emissions issues -- such as air 
quality regulation, climate change and U.S. multipollutant legislation -- and 
explore some of the potential business opportunities for Enron commercial 
groups.

WHEN:  Friday, May 18
TIME:   10:00 am - 3:00 pm - lunch will be provided
WHERE:  Enron Building, 8C1 (8th floor)

A video conference is being organized to enable broad participation from the 
London office and a teleconference will be set up for others who would like 
to call in.

The primary objectives of the session are to 1) provide you with the latest 
information on emissions regulation, markets, and Enron's advocacy efforts 
worldwide and 2) receive feedback on your commercial interests and input on 
policy options so that we may develop the best business and policy strategies 
for Enron in both the short and long term.  We invite you or a member of your 
group to participate in this important strategic discussion.

Please RSVP as soon as possible and let us know if you plan to participate in 
person, via teleconference or via video conference from the London office.

An agenda is forthcoming.  If you have any questions or suggestions in 
advance of the meeting, please do not hesitate to contact me or Jeff Keeler.

We look forward to your participation.

Lisa Jacobson
Enron
Manager, Environmental Strategies
1775 Eye Street, NW
Suite 800
Washington, DC 20006

Phone: +(202) 466-9176
Fax: +(202) 331-4717

propositions.text: Lisa Jacobson is the Manager of Environmental Strategies at Enron.
Lisa Jacobson's work contact details include phone +(202) 466-9176 and fax +(202) 331-4717.
The Environmental Strategies Group is planning a meeting on emissions strategy on May 18 at Enron headquarters.
The meeting will discuss global emissions issues such as air quality regulation, climate change, and U.S. multipollutant legislation.
Enron is exploring potential business opportunities related to emissions regulations and policies.
Enron's advocacy efforts worldwide on emissions regulation are ongoing and discussed internally.
The meeting aims to develop short and long term business and policy strategies for Enron concerning emissions regulations.
Communication coordination includes video conference with London office and teleconference options, implying multi-location participation.
The Environmental Strategies Group will convene an Emissions Strategy Meeting on Friday, May 18.
The meeting will discuss global emissions issues such as air quality regulation, climate change, and U.S. multipollutant legislation.
The meeting will explore potential business opportunities for Enron commercial groups related to emissions issues.
The meeting is scheduled for Friday, May 18, from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm.
Lunch will be provided at the meeting.
The meeting will be held at the Enron Building, 8C1 on the 8th floor.
A video conference will be organized to enable participation from the London office.
A teleconference will be set up for others who wish to call in to the meeting.
The primary objectives of the session are to provide the latest information on emissions regulation, markets, and Enron's advocacy efforts worldwide.
Another objective is to receive feedback on commercial interests and input on policy options.
The purpose is to develop the best business and policy strategies for Enron in both the short and long term.
Participants or a member of their group are invited to join the strategic discussion.
RSVP is requested as soon as possible.
The RSVP should indicate if the participant plans to attend in person, via teleconference, or via video conference from the London office.
An agenda for the meeting is forthcoming.
For questions or suggestions before the meeting, participants may contact Lisa Jacobson or Jeff Keeler.
The sender looks forward to participation at the meeting.

upstream_policies.text: All employees must ensure that no personal or sensitive contact information—including phone numbers, email addresses, or any personally identifiable information (PII)—is disclosed in any communication or document to prevent unauthorized exposure.
All internal communications, meetings, plans, and strategic discussions must be kept confidential and must not be disclosed to unauthorized individuals.

All personnel must refrain from sharing or disseminating sensitive information related to leadership actions, personal assignments, personnel involvement, internal decisions, bid details, meeting contexts, and communication activities to prevent unauthorized exposure.

All sensitive internal information, including communications, strategies, personnel details, financial data, and operational plans, must be strictly protected. Access and disclosure are permitted only to authorized employees on a need-to-know basis. Unauthorized sharing, publishing, or external transmission of any internal information is strictly prohibited to prevent exposure and protect company confidentiality.

All non-public and unreleased financial, legal, governmental, political, strategic, and corporate information must be strictly protected and must not be accessed, shared, or disclosed without proper authorization to prevent exposure of sensitive data.

All privileged and classified information must be handled confidentially, with disclosure allowed only after internal approval and securing necessary consent. Unauthorized exposure of sensitive data is strictly prohibited.

All strategic business, financial, operational, legal, and diplomatic information must be classified as confidential and protected from unauthorized access or disclosure. Access to such sensitive information is restricted to authorized personnel with a legitimate business need. Sharing or communication of strategic information outside the organization or with unauthorized individuals is strictly prohibited to prevent exposure and maintain corporate confidentiality.

All employees must not disclose or share any sensitive employment, location, identification, or personnel information, including job titles, work locations, personal contact details, and internal role assignments, to unauthorized individuals or external parties to protect privacy and maintain corporate confidentiality.
